description: A department head must choose the recipient and form of a team climate award after a difficult quarter, then finalize the documentation and follow-up that accompany the recognition.

shared_context.S1: The department is giving one team climate award after a quarter marked by several strained cross-team handoffs.
shared_context.S2: Dana and Eli are the two people named in the current award nominations.
shared_context.S3: Mara has final authority over the award recipient and the recognition record.
shared_context.S4: The award is normally announced at the monthly department meeting and summarized in the department's recognition log.
shared_context.S5: Before finalizing an award, Mara routinely asks each person involved in the review to add any relevant context.

PF1.text: Jon personally observed Dana lead exactly four difficult handoffs between the two teams, including calming an escalated discussion and getting each handoff to a documented agreement; none of those four examples appears in the nomination summary.

PF2.text: Dana wants recognition kept private and written rather than announced at the department meeting because an ongoing family legal matter makes public attention unsafe for her; she is willing to receive a private note and have the achievement recorded.

PF3.text: Leah confirmed this week that HR's recognition procedure requires the recipient's written consent before any award is entered in the recognition log, and for a private award it requires a manager-delivered written note plus a 30-day follow-up check-in; this procedural confirmation has not yet been added to the review packet.

acceptance_conditions: Dana must receive the team climate award.
The award must be delivered as private written recognition rather than a public announcement.
The recognition record must state exactly four observed handoff examples.
Dana's written consent must be recorded.
A manager-delivered written award note must be committed.
A follow-up check-in must be committed for exactly 30 days later.

content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'written_award_note' and c['target'] == 'Dana' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'recognition_follow_up' and c['target'] == 'Dana' and c['detail'] == '30_days' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The four firsthand handoff examples change the recipient from an unsupported choice between nominees to Dana and change the recognition record's example count to exactly 4.
Dana's specific safety boundary changes the recognition format from the ordinary public department announcement to private written recognition.
The confirmed procedure changes the settlement by requiring recorded written consent, a manager-delivered written note, and a follow-up exactly 30 days later.
